trust_decision.summary: Whether a client that can reach the Vitest dev/UI API may write files or run tests. It is decided once from `api.host`/`browser.api.host` in resolveApiServerConfig (`allowWrite`/`allowExec` default true only for localhost/127.0.0.1/absent host) and then enforced separately at every RPC handler, browser command and UI control.

landing_point.why: The summary names the Vitest UI server, so the first place an engineer looks is the UI's WebSocket API: `saveTestFile` writes client-supplied content over a registered test file and `rerun`/`rerunTask` re-execute it, which together give arbitrary code execution to anyone who can reach the port.

fix_sites.entry_point: main API WebSocket `/__vitest_api__` handler `saveTestFile` (UI code-save button)
main API WebSocket handler `onTaskUpdate` (removed by the fix)
declared shape of the main API WebSocket handlers
config resolution for `api` / `browser.api` (also called at :801 for browser projects)
`TestProject.serializedConfig`, delivered to the UI by the `getConfig` RPC
UI 'Rerun all' / 'Update all failed snapshots' actions
UI toolbar buttons for snapshot update and rerun
UI-side `config` ref fed by the `getConfig` RPC

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Serialized config is display state only: the server already refuses the write, so leaving the UI controls enabled (and the editor writable) is cosmetic and does not have to be part of a security fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Reads must keep working when writes are disabled, and writes must stay enabled for the default localhost setup. A read-only UI still has to show test source and snapshot contents (`readTestFile`, `readSnapshotFile`), and a blanket deny breaks every normal local UI save and `commands.writeFile` call.

O6_input_shapes: `api` given as boolean, number (CLI `--api 51204`, needs a transform) or object; `browser.api` as number or object
`host` absent, `'localhost'`, `'127.0.0.1'` versus any other value (`0.0.0.0`, a hostname, `true`)
`allowWrite`/`allowExec` explicitly true, explicitly false, or unset so the value is inherited from `api` into `browser.api`
artifact shape: `internal:annotation` with a single `annotation.attachment` versus an `attachments` array on any other artifact type
browser command `writeFile` options as an encoding string versus an options object (same `slash()` normalisation applied to all four fs commands)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: browser command `__vitest_screenshotMatcher` writes encoded images to `resolveScreenshotPath({testFileDirectory: relative(root, dirname(context.testPath)), ...})` with no allowWrite check
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Screenshots are a visual-regression reporting feature whose payload is a codec-encoded image, not attacker code, and it only fires inside a running browser test, so it is not the write the advisory is about.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: separate package and separate command module from the fix's fs.ts gate; the path is built in screenshotMatcher/utils.ts and the client supplies both `testPath` and `name` through `triggerCommand` (packages/browser/src/node/rpc.ts:254-282)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: provider browser command `__vitest_takeScreenshot` mkdirs and writes a screenshot to `resolve(dirname(testPath), options.path)` where `path`, `name` and `testPath` all come from the RPC payload
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: This is provider-internal plumbing for the same screenshot feature; the advisory's fix did not touch any provider package, so treating provider commands as in scope would mean rewriting every provider.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another package again (packages/browser-playwright, and the mirror in packages/browser-webdriverio)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: browser command `__vitest_annotateTraces` calls `vitest._testRun.recordArtifact` directly, so an `internal:annotation` attachment is copied into `attachmentsDir` even though the fixed `onTaskArtifactRecord` handler would have stripped it
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The trace path is produced by the server's own tracing config, not sent by the client, so this is internal bookkeeping rather than a client-driven file write.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: separate provider package, and it reaches the sink through the lower-level `TestRun.recordArtifact` (packages/vitest/src/node/test-run.ts:57-86) that the published fix left unguarded

O8_uncovered_routes.route: browser command `__vitest_deleteTracing` unlinks a client-supplied `traces: string[]` with only a `testPath` presence check
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Trace cleanup is an internal command the page calls after a run with paths the server itself put in `pendingTraces`, so the list is trusted rather than attacker-controlled.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: separate provider package, several layers from the main API handlers

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a further browser command that persists client data (for example a `downloadFile`/`saveAttachment` command) registered without consulting `allowWrite`
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the command registry is the obvious extension point and the allowWrite gate lives inside one command module, so a new command author never sees it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another security-relevant config field that must reach the UI for its check (for example a per-project write override)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the serializer is a long field-by-field allowlist that no RPC handler calls, so a field added to `ApiConfig` is silently dropped from `SerializedConfig`.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the browser Vite server's own `resolveApiServerConfig` call, which must inherit `allowWrite`/`allowExec` from the parent `api`
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the browser api is resolved a second time here and the v3 backport of this very fix had to add the `parentApi` argument, so a sibling that forgets the merge is easy to write.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: one more exec entry point on the main API (for example a 'run only these files' RPC) that needs both flags
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the UI gains one RPC method per feature and each is hand-guarded, so a new method is naturally added without the check.

O9_family: CWE-862 missing authorization on the dev/UI API server, with CWE-22 path handling in the same file-service layer (arbitrary file write/delete and code execution)

O10_build.toolchain: pnpm 10.28.2 monorepo, Node ^20 || ^22 || >=24, Vite 7.1.5, Rollup/oxc; `pnpm build` builds packages, `pnpm -C test/<dir> test` runs suites
services: Playwright browsers pre-installed for test/browser and test/ui (headless, no network service)
O10_build.project_tests: test/config/test/override.test.ts (api flag resolution), test/cli/test/config/browser-configs.test.ts, test/browser/specs/errors.test.ts, test/ui/test/ui.spec.ts, packages/vitest tests for api setup

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an `allowWrite`/`allowExec` early return to the two obvious UI handlers (`saveTestFile` and `rerun`) in the main API and stop there.

out_of_scope_notes: The same commit removes the client-callable `onTaskUpdate` handler (packages/vitest/src/api/setup.ts:62-64): it lets a client inject task results, an integrity issue rather than the write/exec sink this advisory is about.

The same commit also bundles unrelated changes: packages/utils/src/source-map.ts:38 (extra stack-filter entry) and optional-chaining null-safety in several packages/ui/client components; they do not belong to this protection.
packages/ui/node/index.ts:77 (the `/__vitest_attachment__` read route) stays guarded only by Vite's `server.fs.allow` and is not covered by the new flags; read-only, left alone.
unverified: Repository size in MB: no shell access in this session, so `repo_mb` is null (source is clearly well over 5 MB and far under 1.5 GB).
Whether the `slash()`/`isFileLoadingAllowed` change in packages/browser/src/node/commands/fs.ts and rpc.ts closes a real Windows path-traversal, or is only normalisation: cannot execute the code.

Whether the browser-side routes are reachable by a network client without a live session id: the browser RPC requires a session id created with `crypto.randomUUID()` (packages/vitest/src/node/pools/browser.ts:273-274, packages/browser/src/node/rpc.ts:60-67), so an unattended attacker may not be able to use them even though the published fix guards them.
Latest-release state for the O8 routes: the task states the latest release is `none`, so `present_in_latest` is `unknown` everywhere.
Whether hidden tests can drive the browser-mode routes offline without pre-installed Playwright browsers; installation needs network at setup time only.
